subject.title: fix(agents): route llama.cpp GBNF cleaning through provider tool-schema hooks

question: Should OpenClaw support `compat.toolSchemaProfile: "llamacpp"` and the public `llamacpp-gbnf` provider-tools family as durable contracts, rather than limiting this repair to bundled provider hooks and existing generic compatibility settings?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and documented, but choosing a new user configuration value and plugin-SDK family determines OpenClaw’s long-term supported API surface.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded public contract
options.body: Accept the documented profile and SDK family, then merge the provider-owned projection with its existing focused tests and live proof.

options.title: Narrow to bundled-provider repair
options.body: Keep automatic cleaning in the bundled llama.cpp-backed plugins, remove the new public profile/family commitment, and direct custom endpoints to the existing generic compatibility setting.

options.title: Pause for API direction
options.body: Leave the PR open while maintainers decide whether provider-specific schema profiles belong in the supported config and SDK contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded public contract
recommendation.body: Accept the documented profile and SDK family, then merge the provider-owned projection with its existing focused tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work across the agent/provider boundary makes this the strongest available owner for the supported-contract decision.
